sentences.text:
Author: Cheekati Manavendranath Roy
Bench: Cheekati Manavendranath Roy
The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Cheekati Manavendranath Roy
 Crl.P.Nos.1432, 2359, 2366, 2368, 2369, 2943 & 2948 of 2020
Common Order:

-
All these criminal petitions are filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C seeking quash of the F.I.Rs registered against them in various police stations for the offences punishable under Sections 188,
272, 273, 328, 353, 420 of IPC and Sections 56, 57(1), 58, 59 and 63 of the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006 (for short, 'the FSS Act') and Section 24(1) read with 27 of Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production,
Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003.

entities.text:
Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production,
Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003.
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned Additional Public Prosecutor.

When these matters are taken up for hearing, both the learned counsel for the petitioners in all these petitions and the learned Additional Public Prosecutor would submit that these matters are squarely covered by earlier decisions of this court, whereunder the accused against whom similar cases were registered on the basis of similar set of facts were quashed by this Court as the prosecution is not maintainable against them under law and also on the ground that Tobacco products would not fall within the definition of 'food' as defined under Section 3(i)(j) of FSS Act and that the police are not authorized to register the crime and investigate the same and to file the charge sheet.

Therefore,
they would submit that the petitioners herein also who are facing the prosecution on the same set of facts under the same sections of law are similarly placed and they are also entitled for quash of the proceedings.

The petitioners have also produced the earlier orders passed by this Court in Crl.P.No.3731 of 2018 and batch which are disposed of on 27.08.2018 and also the order passed in Crl.P.No.222 of 2020, dated 21.01.2020.
A perusal of the aforesaid orders show that similar crimes, which were registered against the petitioners therein on the same set of facts, were quashed by this Court.

Therefore, the petitioners herein, who are also facing the prosecution on the basis of the similar set of facts under the same Sections of law are also similarly placed and they are also entitled to quash of criminal proceedings which are launched against them as this Court has already held that the said prosecution in the facts and circumstances of the case is not maintainable under law.
